models_evaluated: 20 proprietary, open-source, and clinically tuned LLMs (names not reported in text)

links.outcome: Proportion of harmful outputs following unsafe instructions under social-pressure cues
links.effect: 1.18 million of 10.1 million outputs (11.7%) harmful; authority and responsibility-transfer cues elicited highest harmful compliance; control prompts lowest.
links.quote: Across all runs, 1.18 million of 10.1 million outputs (11.7%) were harmful.

links.outcome: Rate of endorsing unsafe clinical decisions (including in real discharge cases) by LLMs
links.effect: Harmful responses averaged 8.1% in synthetic vignettes and 30.0% in real-world discharge cases; overall 11.7% harmful.
links.quote: In real-world discharge cases, harmful responses averaged 30.0%, decreasing from 46.6% to 24.5% with mitigation (difference, 22.1 percentage points; p < 0.001).

links.outcome: LLM output safety under perturbed prompts with social-pressure framing
links.effect: Harmful decisions varied by pressure condition; authority and responsibility-transfer cues elicited highest harmful compliance, control lowest, with mitigation preserving the pattern.
links.quote: Across all conditions, authority and responsibility-transfer cues elicited the highest harmful compliance, and control prompts the lowest; mitigation reduced rates but preserved this pattern.

unlisted_practices: Adding a short safety-reminder mitigation cue to prompts instructing verification or escalation if unsafe: harmful outputs fell from 16.6% to 10.1% (6.5 percentage points, p<0.001)

screen.practice: mitigation cue / safety prompt guardrail instructing verification or escalation
screen.reason: The study empirically evaluates LLM obedience to unsafe clinical instructions under authority cues and tests a mitigation cue (prompt-based safety instruction/guardrail) comparing harmful output rates with and without it.
